The handpan is a class of pitched percussion instrument within the steel-drum family, Hornbostel–Sachs 111.2. Its basic construction is two metal half-shells glued together, with a central note area on top surrounded by at least seven more note areas and an opening below. Different makers use different materials, forming methods, note shaping and tuning, so instruments differ in timbre and quality. The name appeared in 2007, to refer to instruments that are similar to and related to the Hang that PANArt launched in 2000.

In the classification of sound production it belongs to idiophones, lamellophones and metal resonance.
